children: Shares of Upstream Bio rose after the company's treatment for severe asthma met the primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial.
The stock gained 9.3% to $6.57 in premarket trading on Tuesday. Shares were down 78% year to date at market close.

In the trial, the clinical-stage company's verekitug treatment reduced the annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER) across all dose regimens studied in adults with severe asthma, with a 100 milligram dose every 12 weeks reducing AAER by 56% compared to placebo.
The treatment also led to clinically meaningful improvements in lung function and exhaled nitric oxide with every 12-week dosing, the company said.

The results "further strengthen our conviction in verekitug's potential to deliver best-in-class efficacy with the convenience of quarterly dosing, a profile we plan to further evaluate in a broad severe asthma population in phase 3," said Aaron Deykin, chief medical officer and head of research and development.
The company said it remains on track to initiate phase 3 trials in severe asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polypsin in the first quarter of 2027.
